stories.title: Israel's parliament sworn in as Eisenkot tries to forge a government
summary: Israel’s parliament was sworn in on Tuesday without a new government, after a deadlocked general election stripped Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his parliamentary majority but left his main rivals with no clear path to power.
But they have potential allies in Israel’s Arab-led parties, which hold 19 seats and are aligned with Eisenkot in their vehement opposition to Netanyahu.

Eisenkot could secure the threshold with support from Arab-Israeli lawmakers, who secured a record number of seats on the back of anger in the minority community over Netanyahu’s hard-right government.

stories.title: Bilawal calls for unity via ‘political reset’, urges PM to build trust with allies and opposition
summary: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Tuesday called for a “political reset”, wherein all political parties must unite for the sake of the country, while also urging the prime minister to take measures to build trust with the government’s allies and the opposition.

On its part, the Centre has repeatedly cited the KP government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the counterterrorism fight for its decision, following which the PPP’s governor now heads the provincial administration.
As he highlighted the efforts of the Sindh government post the 2022 floods, Bilawal particularly thanked the premier for the Centre’s support in the flood rehabilitation projects.

stories.title: JI says 'basic outline' of proposal for petroleum levy relief agreed upon during talks with govt
summary: ISLAMABAD: Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) Vice Emir Liaqat Baloch said on Tuesday that the government and the party had agreed on the “basic outlines” of a proposed agreement as the two sides held their 10th round of negotiations on petroleum levy relief.

After a meeting with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif last month, both sides agreed to form a bipartisan committee to expand the government’s ongoing fuel relief scheme in response to JI’s demands for the abolition of the petroleum levy.
As per the statement, Baloch said the government also acknowledged that the demand for abolition of the petroleum levy was justified and could result in substantial relief for the public.

stories.title: Pakistan tighten grip on first Test as Sri Lanka struggle at 114-3
summary: Pakistan strengthened their hold on the opening Test against Sri Lanka on Tuesday, declaring their first innings at 434 for nine before reducing the visitors to 114 for three at the close of the second day at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium.
Sri Lanka, who still trail by 320 runs, will resume their innings on the third day with Kamindu Mendis unbeaten on 40 and Dhananjaya de Silva on 22.
Pakistan will resume on the third day firmly in control, with a substantial first-innings lead and three Sri Lankan wickets already in hand.

stories.title: Embattled Pentagon chief slams impeachment effort as 'farce'
summary: Trump has backed Hegseth so far, and on Tuesday wrote on social media that the Pentagon chief “gets an ‘A’ plus, plus, plus for his defence” against the impeachment efforts.

Hegseth on Tuesday defended military interventions in Yemen, Iran and Venezuela as well as strikes targeting alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific. ‘Would do it again’ “I stand behind every one of these operations.
Several of the articles of impeachment relate to the Iran war, accusing Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution, which requires congressional consultation on US military interventions.

stories.title: Centre spent Rs5tr on devolved subjects in violation of Constitution, Senate panel head says
summary: During a meeting of that sub-committee last month, senators sought a probe into a staggering Rs2.6 trillion expenditure by the federal government on education and health ministries.

The FIA informed the committee that 512 notices had been issued to various companies in connection with the ongoing investigation, out of which 19 companies joined the proceedings with partial records, while more than 100 notices were returned or remained undelivered.

The panel was also briefed about the FBR’s reluctance to share relevant records with the parliamentary committee, particularly when the department was prepared to provide information to the court and other authorities.

stories.title: TV anchor's killing: Court extends physical remand of victim's husband by 4 days
summary: RAWALPINDI: The physical remand of the husband of anchorperson Rabia Ahsan, who was shot dead at home in the Gulshanabad area earlier in the week, was extended by four days by a court on Tuesday.
He urged the court to extend the remand by seven days in order to interrogate the suspect and complete the investigation.
The court subsequently extended the remand by four days to facilitate the investigation and directed the investigating officer to produce the accused on Nov 14.

stories.title: Imran's hospital transfer: Uzma seeks early fixation of contempt plea against govt for third time
summary: The SC’s office has already turned down Uzma’s two previous requests for an early hearing of the contempt plea, which was filed on Aug 22.

The application stated the previous contempt plea had also sought court directives to arrange and facilitate weekly meetings between Imran and his family members, including petitioners and his other sisters, Noreen Niazi and Aleema Khan, along with his cousin Qasim Zaman.

On Sept 16, resuming the hearing on petitions concerning Imran’s health, the SC had expressed reservations over the Federal Constitutional Court’s (FCC) directive that cases pertaining to the PTI founder’s hospital transfer be fixed before it.

stories.title: Britain says its bases are safe after US refuelling planes evacuated
summary: Britain said on Tuesday that its military bases were safe, after the US removed huge refuelling aircraft from a British airbase following what the Wall Street Journal said was a threat from Iran, the second such apparent evacuation in three months.
In September, the US removed bombers that had been used to strike Iran from another British base, RAF Fairford, on security grounds after a group of men approached the base in white vans.

The US upgraded the security posture at RAF Mildenhall and another UK base, RAF Lakenheath, to FPCON Charlie, the second-highest defensive threat level, the Wall Street Journal report said, citing a US official familiar with the matter.

stories.title: Lawyer says Shah Mahmood Qureshi taken to hospital days after suffering fall
summary: LAHORE: The lawyer representing Shah Mahmood Qureshi said on Tuesday that the senior PTI leader, who is currently incarcerated at Kot Lakhpat jail, was taken to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC) days after suffering a fall.
Speaking to Dawn, his counsel Rana Mudassar Umar said: “[Qureshi] was taken to PIC today as he fainted and suffered a fall a few days ago.
On Nov 6, a meeting of the PTI core committee also expressed concern over Qureshi’s “fall and the resulting impact on his health”.

stories.title: Wapda says no threat to Tarbela Dam's integrity, critical structures after rock collapse at project site
summary: The consultants, contractor and Wapda project management briefed him on the current situation and the measures taken so far,” it said.
According to the handout, the Wapda chairman directed the consultants to submit a detailed report covering all aspects of the incident at the earliest.

He further directed the consultants, contractor and Wapda project team to execute remedial measures immediately, and to finalise the contingency plan to minimise the delay in the overall completion of the project due to the incident.

stories.title: Lahore’s PM2.5 level eight times WHO guideline, report says
summary: Lahore’s average PM2.5 concentration stood at 126 micrograms per cubic metre during the period, exceeding the 24-hour National Environmental Quality Standards (NEQS) on all 40 days for which valid data were available.

Lahore’s average PM2.5 concentration between 6pm on Nov 8 and 1am on Nov 10 was 234 micrograms per cubic metre, 10pc higher than the average recorded during the same hours over the preceding seven days.
The average increase in the four border cities — Lahore, Kasur, Sialkot and Narowal — was 36 micrograms per cubic metre, compared with 85 micrograms in Faisalabad and Multan.

stories.title: Political narratives and allegations have a limited 'shelf life', CM Maryam says
summary: JHELUM: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Tuesday said political narratives, allegations and criticism had a limited “shelf life”, asserting that public service and development work ultimately determined electoral success.

She said she was answerable to the people for the expenditure of public money, adding that she would not spare any minister or official against whom evidence of corruption or bribery was presented. “I have not said that corruption has completely ended in Punjab,” she said.
On Friday, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif claimed that Salik’s recent corruption allegations against the Punjab government are part of efforts to set the ground for an “alternative arrangement”.

stories.title: Extreme heat
summary: Rural women, who undertake considerable agricultural and household work, face prolonged exposure to extreme temperatures.
Without tweaking policies to respond to the climate challenge, repeated heatwaves will erode productivity, making farming less viable for smallholders.
Heat is already cutting into rural incomes and into what families can afford to eat.

stories.title: Missing discussion
summary: IN contrast to official claims of economic stability, a series of recently released reports provide disturbing evidence of deepening poverty and a human development crisis in Pakistan.

The UNDP’s 2025 Global Multidimensional Poverty Index reported that 38.3pc of Pakistan’s population (95m people) is multidimensionally poor — deprived not just of cash but also of necessities such as healthcare and education.
The UNDP’s Human Development Report 2025 placed Pakistan 168th out of 193 countries appearing in the ‘low’ human development category.

stories.title: BHC hands ex-MPA Abdul Majeed Achakzai 10-year sentence in traffic cop hit-and-run case
summary: QUETTA: The Balochistan High Court on Tuesday handed former MPA Abdul Majeed Achakzai a ten-year sentence in a case regarding the death of a traffic policeman in a hit-and-run incident.

A division bench comprising Justice Muhammad Amir Nawaz Rana and Justice Abdul Qayyum Lehr allowed an appeal filed by the provincial government against Achakzai’s acquittal and set aside the local court decision dated September 4, 2020.
However, in 2020, a local court in Quetta acquitted him in the case.

stories.title: Nvidia's clubby board faces a sticky 'honey pot' test
summary: China's Foreign Ministry said the spying claim was "a groundless accusation, slander, and a smear." Nvidia co-founder Huang, 63, has ​no obvious successor and close ties to Trump.
Political economy Yale University management professor Jeffrey Sonnenfeld said the company faces additional national-security questions because of the ties between Huang and Trump.
Last ⁠year the ​Trump administration allowed Nvidia to resume certain China shipments under arrangements in which the US ​government receives a cut of the company's China chip sales.

stories.title: School bus overturns near Murree, killing driver, injuring 30
summary: A school bus carrying students and staff overturned near Shawala on the Expressway Link Road near Murree, killing the driver and injuring 30 students and staff members.
Teams from Rescue 1122 Murree rushed to the scene after receiving information about the accident and launched a rescue operation.
Rescuers pulled the injured passengers from the wreckage, provided them with first aid and shifted 30 students and staff members to the Tehsil Headquarters Hospital in Murree.

stories.title: £190m corruption case: IHC adjourns hearing for 10 days, orders meeting between Imran and legal team
summary: Justice Dogar observed that Khosa would argue the main appeals and directed the advocate general to facilitate his meeting with Imran.

Justice Dogar, however, observed that the matter relating to Bushra’s medical treatment was pending before the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) and that Barrister Safdar could pursue the issue of access to his clients before the appropriate forum.
The court further allowed Barrister Safdar to meet Imran and Bushra before adjourning the proceedings for 10 days.

stories.title: Australia to mandate AI breach reporting, create regulator after OpenAI breach
summary: Australia will require artificial intelligence companies to report breaches ‌and consider changes to criminal law to address "serious misconduct", Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Tuesday, after an OpenAI agent broke into a government website.
Albanese said his government had accepted all recommendations of the ​review.
The mandatory AI safety and ​security protections will form part of the government's proposed AI legislation, Albanese said, which it plans to introduce in ​Parliament next year.

stories.title: Bangladesh prosecutor says ex-PM Sheikh Hasina will be executed if she returns
summary: The daughter of a revolutionary who led Bangladesh to independence in 1971, Hasina presided over breakneck economic growth, helping transform the South Asian nation of 170 million people from a largely agricultural economy into a global manufacturing hub.
Hasina has repeatedly said she intends to return to Bangladesh in December, telling AFP she is “fully aware” she faces being hanged if she returns.

Extradition process Hasina defied orders from the court to return to Bangladesh to attend her trial last year on whether she bore command responsibility for the bloody crackdown on the student-led uprising.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz performs dome placement ceremony at Chashma nuclear plant
summary: Addressing the ceremony, the prime minister described the dome placement as a historic occasion at Pakistan's largest nuclear power plant, which was built in close collaboration with China.

He also praised the engineers, technicians and workers from both Pakistan and China for their contributions. #BREAKING Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif says Chashma-V will be Pakistan’s largest nuclear power plant, addressing its dome placement ceremony.
The prime minister thanked China for its support in building the power plant, saying Chashma-5 was the seventh nuclear power unit Beijing had helped construct in Pakistan.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz departs for Turkiye, to address COP31 tomorrow
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif left for Antalya, Turkiye, on Tuesday for a visit from Nov 10-12 to attend the Leaders’ Summit of the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP 31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

Negotiators had been locked in discussions late on Sunday over demands by developing nations to include items on climate finance in the official agenda. “This has already been a difficult start for COP31,” said Jasper Inventor, head of Greenpeace’s COP31 delegation.

Inventor said developed countries were “taking a hard line” over whether to include a platform, agreed at COP30 in Brazil last year, aimed at discussing how wealthy nations should provide funds to developing nations.

stories.title: Tariq Fazal defends Imran's medical treatment amid renewed concerns
summary: Speaking to reporters at the Parliament House, Chaudhry said that Barrister Salman Safdar had himself acknowledged that medical check-up facilities were "available" to Imran during a media talk outside Islamabad High Court earlier in the day.
The Supreme Court on August 18 had ordered that the PTI founder be shifted to Islamabad's Shifa International Hospital within two days for medical examination and treatment.
The government has also previously rejected claims that Imran was being denied proper medical care.

stories.title: Trump says Nvidia CEO Huang had 'no idea' lover was alleged Chinese spy
summary: US President Donald Trump took a tech tone towards Jensen Huang on Monday, saying the Nvidia CEO was “suffering greatly” and didn’t know a woman he had an affair with was an alleged Chinese spy.

Trump also danced around the question of when he personally was aware of intelligence linking the chip boss to Alice Huang, a Chinese executive who had allegedly been funnelling information to Beijing.
Trump said he was not aware of the allegations when Huang accompanied him to China in May.

stories.title: Matric exams postponed in North Waziristan due to security situation
summary: BANNU: The Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE), Bannu, has postponed the Secondary School Certificate Second Annual Examination in North Waziristan due to the security situation while a curfew has also been imposed in the district’s Mir Ali area.
In North Waziristan, this is the second time that these exams — scheduled to start on October 12 — have been postponed.
He further stated that residents wishing to travel outside North Waziristan could use the Miranshah, Isha and Razmak routes.

stories.title: Who is Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman tied to Nvidia's CEO?
summary: Megaspeed attracted public attention in October 2025, when the New York Times reported the company was under US investigation over whether it was helping Chinese customers obtain advanced Nvidia chips subject to Washington's export controls.
Alice Huang has since been thrust into the spotlight because of her links with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
A Hexi business card reviewed by Reuters identified Alice Huang ​as a partner and general manager, with an office in Shanghai's Lujiazui financial district.

stories.title: Wapda chairman orders inquiry into Tarbela project incident
summary: The consultants, contractor and WAPDA's project management team briefed him on the prevailing situation and the measures taken so far.
WAPDA Chairman Lt Gen Muhammad Saeed (Retd) has ordered a departmental inquiry and immediate remedial measures following a tunnel incident at the 1,530MW Tarbela Fifth Extension Hydropower Project.

He also instructed the consultants, contractor and WAPDA's project team to immediately implement rehabilitation measures and finalise an emergency response plan to minimise any potential delays in the overall completion of the project.

stories.title: Fact check: Viral video does not show a man kicking and damaging Tarbela Dam; it’s old and unrelated
summary: How it starting On Nov 9, an Afghan propaganda account, based on its past posts, shared a video on X, allegedly showing a man standing at the edge of the Tarbela Dam’s wall and kicking it, highlighting the poor condition.

A keyword search was conducted to verify whether any credible media outlets in Pakistan had recently reported on a viral video of a man kicking the walls of the Tarbela Dam and breaking them easily, but it yielded no results.
Fact-check status: False The claim that a viral video shows a man kicking and damaging Tarbela Dam is false.

stories.title: Israeli forces shoot dead 14-year-old in West Bank: Palestinian officials
summary: Israeli forces shot dead a 14-year-old in the occupied West Bank, Palestinian officials said, with Israel claiming it was responding to stone-throwing.
On October 23, Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint near Hebron before being killed by Israeli forces, who later responded with a major operation in the flashpoint city.
Israeli soldiers or settlers have killed at least 1,116 Palestinians in the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war, according to an AFP tally based on Palestinian Authority figures.

stories.title: Anthropic unveils new Fable, Mythos models as competition heats up ahead of IPO
summary: Anthropic on Monday unveiled two new artificial intelligence models, Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, as the OpenAI rival seeks to strengthen its position in the fast-growing AI market ahead of its planned initial public offering (IPO).
The company said Claude Fable 5.2 was designed for coding, reasoning and AI agent tasks, while Claude Mythos 5.2 was developed for approved cybersecurity and life-sciences research applications.

Access to Claude Mythos 5.2 will be restricted to organisations approved through Anthropic’s verification programmes for cybersecurity and life-sciences research, while Claude Fable 5.2 will be available more broadly, the company said.

stories.title: Trump nominates Natalie Baker for US ambassador to Pakistan
summary: US President Donald Trump has nominated Natalie Baker, the current charge d’affaires at the US embassy in Islamabad, to be the ambassador to Pakistan, according to a statement by the White House.
She had arrived in Islamabad as deputy chief of mission in August 2024, according to details available on the embassy’s website.

Baker was also deployed as the deputy chief of mission and charge d’affaires of the US Mission to Libya, deputy director of the Iran Regional Presence Office at the US consulate in Dubai and economic counsellor at the US embassy in Kuwait.

stories.title: Trump sets off bedlam in White House briefing room with UFC chief's appearance
summary: President Donald Trump set off a scramble in the White House press briefing room on Monday with an appearance so sudden that aides had no time to place the presidential seal on the podium.
After heavy Republican losses in the midterm elections less than a week ago, Trump announced on Saturday that he had offered the White House press secretary job to White.

Trump said on Sunday he was just teasing, but White came to the White House anyway to see the president. “Everyone please take a seat in the briefing room RIGHT NOW,” was a press assistant’s urgent instruction for reporters over the loudspeaker.

stories.title: Bilawal rejects corruption allegations in Sindh housing project, accuses opponents of smear campaign
summary: Referring to relations between the federal and provincial governments, he recalled that a former prime minister had told the PPP that Sindh did not belong to his government.

One million homes completed for flood victims Highlighting the Sindh People's Housing Scheme, Bilawal described it as the world's largest housing project and said the provincial government had completed one million homes for flood-affected families.

Also read: 'We will fix it': Bilawal says if system has failed, hand Islamabad to Tharparkar The PPP chairman said the World Bank had expressed confidence in the Sindh government and released funds for the housing project.

stories.title: Paul McCartney reaches historic financial milestone joining elite billionaire club
summary: The financial publication attributed McCartney's wealth to several income streams, including music publishing, songwriting royalties, touring, business interests and his extensive art collection.
McCartney also benefits from the continuing commercial success of the Beatles.
The musician reportedly earns around $10 million annually from his share of Beatles songwriting copyrights, which he spent years fighting to reclaim.

stories.title: 63 students hospitalised after fire at religious school in Bangladesh
summary: At least 63 students were hospitalised after a fire broke out at an Islamic religious school in Bangladesh's central Narayanganj district early Tuesday, a fire official told Anadolu.
Four firefighting units were dispatched and brought the blaze under control, he said, adding that most students escaped without burns, although several suffered from smoke inhalation.
Read: Building fire kills 14 in China's northern city of Taiyuan All 63 affected students were taken to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka.

stories.title: James Gunn breaks silence on four-year run at DC Studios
summary: James Gunn has opened up about the personal and professional challenges of leading DC Studios, describing his four-year tenure as a rewarding but demanding experience.
The decision brought an end to Gunn and Safran's four-year leadership of the studio.
The filmmaker's departure marks a significant change for DC Studios, although projects developed during his leadership are expected to continue.

stories.title: Pindi court extends husband's physical remand by four days in journalist Rabia Ahsan's murder case
summary: A Rawalpindi court on Tuesday extended the physical remand of Ahsan Tahir, husband of television anchorperson and journalist Rabia Ahsan, by four days in connection with her murder.
The court on Monday had granted police a one-day physical remand of the suspect.
The court directed police to complete the investigation and produce the suspect before it again on November 13.
